Thanks again for the quick demo last week. We're moving toward a pilot and our security/compliance team sent over a short checklist (attached) with a few must-haves before we can sign the PO:

TL;DR — we can cover most asks with a phased approach. Details below.

Phase 0 (today):
- Per-request audit logging exists; we can generate tenant-scoped export bundles (NDJSON/CSV) on demand for up to 90 days. We can surface API-driven exports and sign them.
- KMS: we support Redwood-managed keys today. We have an existing design for CMK (customer-managed KMS) but full end-to-end attestation + rotation logs are on the near-term roadmap (Q1-Q2 2027).
- SSO/access evidence: we can provide SAML/OIDC config snapshots and login audit logs for the last 90 days from our auth infra. 12 months require retention tiering.

Phase 1 (30–60 days):
- Add scheduled retention tiers (7/90/365) exportable to S3 or pushed to customer SIEM. This requires a small infra task and an API flag. Estimate: 3–4 engineer-weeks (Marcus).
- CMK exception path: short-term workaround is an encrypted key escrow. We can implement a documented manual process for customers to upload a wrapped key and a signed attestation; not fully automated.

Phase 2 (Q1 2027):
- Fully automated CMK with rotation logs in audit stream + attestation artifacts for auditors.
- 12-month audit-log retention in cold storage with on-demand rehydration and evidence packaging.

Evidence we need from ArcadiaPay to scope the work:
- Expected retention SLAs per environment (prod/staging).
- SIEM ingestion format preference (CSV vs NDJSON), sample schema.
- Whether CMK must be HSM-backed and if ArcadiaPay's KMS provider requires a specific wrapping algorithm.

Attachments: proposed-exception-flow.v1.png (sketch of the manual escrow workaround).

Neha Kapoor
Head of Security Engineering

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Agree with the phased plan. A couple of engineering clarifications/asks from infra:

1) Retention tiers: we need to confirm whether ArcadiaPay expects immutable retention (append-only) or soft-delete with retained metadata. Immutable retention requires object-lock style storage and will add ~10% cost + QA.

2) Export format: NDJSON preferred (streaming friendly). If they want CSV we need a converter job; cost estimate ~1 engineer-week.

3) CMK: the manual escrow workaround is feasible for pilot. If they require HSM-backed CMK, we need vendor onboarding (YubiHSM, AWS KMS external key store) — add 3–6 weeks.

Estimate to deliver Phase 1 (scheduling + 90/365 retention + export hooks + manual CMK escrow docs): ~4 engineer-weeks across infra and platform with one sprint of QA. We can allocate a small project lane if sales confirms pilot commitment (Ben).

Marcus Lin
Director, Platform Engineering
